name: Tech office
description: A modern startup campus at golden hour: glass and graphite, and a document window for every conversation.

text.headquarters-empty: The office floor is empty: no coordinator is running.
text.register-greeting: {here} napping here{upstairs}. Who should I wake?
text.register-empty: Every couch is free: nobody is napping right now.
text.letter-for-sleeper: {name} is napping in the lounge: the message waits until it wakes.
text.rookery-greeting: {waiting}Want me to send something for you?
text.rookery-empty: Nothing has gone out yet today. Want me to send something?
text.end-session-after: Its pane closes and it goes to the lounge to nap; you can wake it there.
text.session-ended: {name}'s session ended; it goes to the lounge to nap.
text.conversation-asleep: {name} is napping in the lounge. Wake it to talk; it opens in a new terminal window.
text.quest-greeting: You have {count} tickets assigned. Pick one, or search across every project.
text.quest-greeting-one: You have one ticket assigned. Or search across every project.
text.quest-empty: Nothing is assigned to you right now. Search finds any ticket.
text.quest-signed-out: I need your Atlassian sign-in to pull your tickets. Add it in Settings.
text.quest-search: Search all tickets by text or key
text.library-greeting: All of Confluence is searchable from here. What are you looking for?
text.library-signed-out: Connect your Atlassian account in Settings to search the wiki.
text.library-recent-empty: Pages you open here show up in this list.
text.crier-greeting: {count} channels have unread messages. Search all of Slack, messages or channels, and I'll pull it up.
text.crier-quiet: You're all caught up. Search all of Slack and I'll pull it up.
text.crier-signed-out: I'm not connected to Slack yet. Sign in and I can pull up any channel.
text.forge-greeting: Everything on the benches is yours or your team's. Which one should we look at?
text.forge-empty: The benches are clear: nothing of yours or your team's is open on GitHub.
text.recruit-worker-greeting: Need another engineer on the team? Give them a name, a repo, and their first ticket.
text.recruit-independent-greeting: Looking for a freelancer? Tell me who, which repo, and the brief. They don't report to anyone.
text.recruit-joined: {name} accepted the offer and is onboarding.

pet.name: Office corgi
pet.examine: {name}, the campus corgi. Head of morale, reports to nobody.

cat-grey.name: Grey cat
cat-grey.examine: {name}, a grey cat asleep somewhere warm. It has commit access to the sofa.

parrot.name: Green parrot
parrot.examine: {name}, the mailroom parrot. Repeats every subject line it hears.

hamster.name: Hamster
hamster.examine: {name}, the library hamster, cheeks full of sunflower seeds and secrets.

hedgehog.name: Hedgehog
hedgehog.examine: {name}, the lab's hedgehog. Curls into a ball whenever a build fails.

bell.name: Desk bell
bell.examine: A chrome desk bell. Ding for service, ding for joy.

handbell.name: Handbell
handbell.examine: A brass handbell for stand-ups that run long.

light.name: Desk lamp
light.examine: An adjustable desk lamp in teal, with a warm bulb.

box.name: Espresso machine
box.examine: A tiny espresso machine. The most important server in the building.

candle.name: Reading lamp
candle.examine: A brushed-steel reading lamp, always on.

tome.name: Tablet
tome.examine: A tablet with a keyboard cover, still logged in to someone's notes.
lines: "TODO: write the TODO list."
"Retro notes: more snacks, fewer meetings."
"Idea: a dashboard for the dashboards."
"Reminder: water the plants (the real ones)."
"It works on my machine. Ship it?"

spin.name: Fidget spinner
spin.examine: A three-armed fidget spinner on a little wooden stand.

barista.name: Theo the barista
barista.examine: A barista who can read the state of a sprint from the coffee orders.
lines: Oat, almond, or the one that's basically water we charge extra for?
I can tell how a sprint's going by the orders. Today is a triple-shot kind of day.
Your name on the cup? I'll spell it creatively. It's my art form.
Between us, the decaf pot is a myth. Everyone knows. Nobody says.
This espresso machine has better uptime than production. Don't tell the on-call.
reactions: Whoa, one order at a time! I've got two hands and one milk frother.
Okay, I'm putting you down for 'surprise me'.
barks: Fresh pot! Get it while it's hot.

facilities.name: Dana from Facilities
facilities.examine: Dana from Facilities, a ladder on her shoulder and a ticket queue in her head.
lines: A light flickering isn't a ghost. It's ticket four-oh-four. I'm on it.
Someone keeps setting the thermostat to 'arctic'. I will find you.
The ladder is not a standing desk. I've had to say that more than once.
Every plant in this plaza has a name. That one's Gerald. Say hi to Gerald.
Please stop microwaving fish. I'm asking nicely. For now.
reactions: Did you file a ticket? You did not file a ticket.
Hold that thought, my radio's... no, that's just you.

visitor.name: Sam the visitor
visitor.examine: A visitor with a lanyard, a confident smile, and no idea where the lobby is.
lines: Hi! I'm here for the nine o'clock. It's... half past eleven? Oh no.
Is it normal for everyone here to talk to their laptops?
Reception gave me a badge and a smile. I still have the smile.
I followed the smell of solder to the hardware lab and ended up at the cafe. Not complaining.
Everyone's so friendly. Someone gave me a sticker. I have nine stickers now.
reactions: Sorry! Am I in your way? I feel like I'm in everyone's way.
Do you work here? Could you badge me in? Please?

dogwalker.name: Priya the dog walker
dogwalker.examine: The office dog walker, holding a leash with nobody on the end of it.
lines: Have you seen Waffles? Corgi, this tall, extremely confident? I looked away for one second.
Office dogs are great for morale. Mine is great for morale and for stealing croissants.
I walk six dogs a day round this plaza. My step count is the stuff of legend.
Yes, the leash is empty. Long story. It probably ends at the snack table.
Dogs always know who's had too many meetings. They sit with them. It's a service.
reactions: Is that a treat in your pocket? No? Waffles will be crushed.
Okay, okay, I'll check by the planters. Again.
barks: Who's a good... where'd he go?

maya.name: Maya the product manager
maya.examine: A product manager with a coffee, a roadmap, and a sticky note on her sleeve she hasn't noticed.
lines: Quick sync? Two minutes. I said that about the last meeting, and I meant it then too.
I've moved this sticky note across the wall four times. It's in 'Next' now. Emotionally, it's 'Later'.
Every roadmap is a guess with nice colours. Mine has the nicest colours.
What problem are we solving? I ask it so often my coffee order is just 'the user'.
I love a good retro. Mostly for the snacks. Also the learnings. Mostly the snacks.
reactions: Let's take this offline. By offline I mean over there, by the coffee.
Love the energy! Can you put it in a ticket?
barks: Who has the big meeting room?

kai.name: Kai the SRE
kai.examine: The SRE on call this week, still in a cycling helmet, ready to sprint to a server that isn't here.
lines: I'm on call. It's quiet. Don't say it's quiet. Oh no, I said it's quiet.
The helmet stays on. You never know when you'll need to sprint to a rack. We're in the cloud, but still.
Three things I believe in: monitoring, runbooks, and a bike ride after a long night.
Every outage teaches you something. Mostly that someone once wrote 'TODO: handle this later'.
My pager has a ringtone. I heard it in my sleep last night. It was the kettle.
reactions: Is that a page? Was that a page? Oh. It's you.
Easy! My heart rate is already on a dashboard somewhere.

jo.name: Jo the office manager
jo.examine: The office manager, apron on from restocking the kitchen, who knows where every spare charger lives.
lines: Snacks restocked, plants watered, and someone has once again taken all the good pens.
Lost a charger? Third drawer, left side, behind the forty other chargers people lost.
Please label your lunch. 'Mine' is not a label. Everyone thinks it's theirs.
The meeting rooms are named after planets. Pluto is the small one. We don't talk about Pluto.
Cake at three! Whose birthday? Doesn't matter. Cake at three.
reactions: I'm one person with one label maker. Pace yourself.
If this is about the thermostat, I've heard. Everyone's heard.

juniper.name: Juniper the design intern
juniper.examine: The design intern, laptop open and scarf on, nudging a button one pixel left and back again.
lines: Does this button look friendly to you? I moved it one pixel left. It feels braver now.
I made forty icons today. Thirty-nine are arrows. I've become an arrow person.
My mentor says whitespace is a feature. I'm learning to love the nothing.
I named my colour palette 'Sunday morning'. Everyone pretends that's normal. Thank you.
Is it okay to have opinions about fonts as an intern? Asking for me. I have many.
reactions: Ah! Sorry, I was in the zone. The kerning zone.
Hold still? I'm sketching you as a user persona.

marco.name: Marco the office chef
marco.examine: The office chef, hat high and spoon ready, who believes no problem survives a good soup.
lines: Today's special: lentil soup, and a gentle reminder to look away from the screen once an hour.
Nobody argues over a good lasagna. Well, they do, but more kindly.
I put the cookies out at four. At four-oh-two there are no cookies. Every day.
Food is a feature. I ship it daily, and I've never once had to roll it back.
Try the chili. It's mild. I say that and someone always cries. Happily, I hope.
reactions: Ah, a hungry one! Lunch is at noon, my friend, not now.
Hands off the tiramisu. It's resting. Like you should.

rex.name: Rex the lunch-run captain
rex.examine: A colleague in a headband who has turned the lounge into the start line of the lunchtime run.
lines: Lunch run at noon! Five kilometres, or one, or a brisk walk to the sandwich place. All welcome.
Standing desks are great. Walking desks are greater. Running desks are a lawsuit.
Hydrate! You, me, the plants. Everybody hydrates.
I took a call on the treadmill once. Never again. Everyone thought I was panicking.
Stretch your wrists, roll your shoulders. Your keyboard will thank you. Silently.
reactions: You're keen! Love it. Warm up first, though.
Whoa, pace yourself! It's a marathon, not a... it's a marathon.
barks: Lunch run at noon, who's in?
